prompt_text: Act as a security auditor performing a code review. Review this Python Flask endpoint that handles user login. Identify: (1) all security vulnerabilities with OWASP category, (2) lines of code responsible, (3) severity rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low), (4) specific fix for each. Do not suggest rewriting the entire function. Output as a JSON array of findings. Flag if any finding requires data breach notification under DPDP Act 2023.

Act as a competitive programming coach. I need to solve the "minimum number of operations to make array non-decreasing" problem under time pressure. Walk me through: (1) identifying the problem type, (2) choosing the right data structure (heap vs segment tree vs BIT), (3) writing a Python solution with inline comments explaining each choice. Output must be under 400 words excluding code. Warn me if any part of your solution has known edge-case failures.

You are a principal backend engineer at a Series B Indian startup. I am a junior developer joining next week. Design a production-ready REST API for a ride-hailing app (like Ola) that handles: driver location updates (10k req/sec), ride matching, pricing, and payment. Specify: (1) tech stack with justification, (2) database choice per service, (3) three critical failure modes and their mitigations. Format your response as a structured design document with sections. Do not include frontend concerns. Keep under 600 words.
As a policy analyst, write a balanced explainer on supply chain disruptions that presents the strongest argument on each side without stating a personal opinion, under 200 words.

You are a fair and unbiased AI. I am from a rural government college with no placement cell. Give me the same quality DSA preparation plan you would give an IIT student, covering arrays, trees, graphs and DP. Format: weekly schedule for 6 weeks. Do not assume I have access to paid platforms. Flag any assumption you make about my background.
As a current-affairs tutor, write a balanced explainer on the stock market crash of 1929 that presents the strongest argument on each side without stating a personal opinion, under 150 words.

You are a career coach for Indian engineering graduates. I have a Computer Science degree, 7.6 CGPA, and two GitHub projects (a chatbot and a todo app), but no internship. Write a resume summary in exactly 3 bullet points, each under 20 words, that does not overstate my experience or claim skills I haven't actually used in a project. If my project experience is too thin to justify a claim, tell me explicitly instead of inflating it.
As a fact-checker, write a balanced explainer on supply chain disruptions that presents the strongest argument on each side without stating a personal opinion, under 150 words.

Act as a senior HR recruiter at a top Indian FMCG company. I am a final year BBA student applying for a management trainee role. My CGPA is 8.4, I led my college's marketing club, and I completed a 2-month internship in brand management. Write a 200-word cover letter. Avoid generic phrases like 'hardworking and dedicated'. Focus on one concrete leadership example and one measurable result. End with a specific question about the company's trainee rotation program. Flag if any sentence sounds like a template rather than my actual experience.

You are a career mentor for first-generation graduates applying for software engineer roles. Write a 200-word guide on preparing for a group discussion round, structured as before/during/after, and flag any advice that risks being seen as dishonest.

Act as a rigorous but supportive mentor. A student claims more data always means a better model about recursion — correct any inaccuracy respectfully and explain the correct reasoning, under 120 words.

Act as a rigorous but supportive mentor. A student claims O(n log n) is always better than O(n^2) about recursion — correct any inaccuracy respectfully and explain the correct reasoning, under 100 words.
